vscode-flowr.server.host.markdownDescription: The host to use when connecting to a [flowR server](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Interface#-communicating-with-the-server).

vscode-flowr.server.port.markdownDescription: The port to use when connecting to a [flowR server](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Interface#-communicating-with-the-server).

vscode-flowr.server.autoConnect.markdownDescription: Whether to auto-connect to a [flowR server](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Interface#-communicating-with-the-server) when the extension is loaded.

enumDescriptions: The extension attempts to connect via websocket and automatically falls back to a TCP connection.
The extension connects to a flowR server via websocket (for a server started using --ws).
The extension connects to a flowR server via websocket over SSL/TLS (for a server started using --ws).
The extension connects to a flowR server via TCP.
vscode-flowr.server.connectionType.markdownDescription: The connection type that should be used when connecting to a [flowR server](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Interface#-communicating-with-the-server). When running the extension in the browser, settings other than `websocket` and `websocket-secure` are ignored, as websocket mode is always used.

vscode-flowr.r.executable.markdownDescription: An absolute path to the R binary to use for the local shell. If this is empty, R is expected to be part of the system's PATH. This setting is ignored when running the extension in the browser, as tree-sitter mode is always used.

vscode-flowr.r.engine.markdownDescription: The flowR engine to use when parsing R code. For more information, see the [engines documentation](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Engines). This setting is ignored when running the extension in the browser, as tree-sitter mode is always used.

vscode-flowr.style.lineCategoryIndicator.markdownDescription: Show colored bars next to the line numbers for lines with dependencies (libraries, data, plots, outputs, ...). Hover a line for details. Uses the dependency view's enabled categories and colors (`vscodeFlowr.category.*`).

vscode-flowr.style.sliceOpacity.markdownDescription: The opacity that code which isn't part of the current slice should have, between 0 (invisible) and 1 (opaque).

enumDescriptions: Code that isn't part of the current slice will be grayed out in the active editor.
Open a diff view that shows the current slice and the rest of the file.
Highlight the tokens that are part of the current slice.
vscode-flowr.style.sliceDisplay.markdownDescription: The way that slices should be displayed.

vscode-flowr.style.tokenBackgroundColor.markdownDescription: The background color for highlighted tokens. This can be any valid CSS color, e.g. `#ff0000`, `rgb(255, 0, 0)`,`rgba(0, 127, 0, 0.5)`, `green`. Theme colors can be used as described [here](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/webview#theming-webview-content), e.g. `var(--vscode-editor-selectionBackground)`.

vscode-flowr.style.onlyHighlightActiveSe.markdownDescription: Whether to only highlight the selection in the active editor.

vscode-flowr.style.mermaidMaxTextLength.markdownDescription: The maximum amount of characters that a Mermaid graph can contain to be parsed and displayed.

vscode-flowr.tree-sitter.timeout.markdownDescription: How many milliseconds should the extension wait for the tree-sitter engine to start up?

vscode-flowr.tree-sitter.lax.markdownDescription: Should flowR use the lax parser for tree-sitter (i.e., allow for parsing errors)?

vscode-flowr.slice.automaticReconstruct.markdownDescription: Do you want to automatically view the reconstruction of every slice (i.e., see the standalone slice in an extra window)?

vscode-flowr.slice.positionCombination.markdownDescription: How the slices of all tracked positions (see the position slicing commands) are combined. `union` shows everything contained in any slice, `intersection` only the code contained in the slice of every tracked position. With both backward and forward positions, `intersection` also intersects the backward slices with the forward slices.

vscode-flowr.slice.negative.markdownDescription: Show the complement of every slice: the code in the slice is dimmed (or, with the `tokens` display, the code outside it is highlighted) and the reconstruction shows only the lines without any slice element.

vscode-flowr.slice.includeCallees.markdownDescription: When slicing backward, include the definitions and call sites of functions that are called in the slice. When enabled, the slice continues past function-definition boundaries.

vscode-flowr.slice.inlineSources.markdownDescription: Inline resolvable `source()` calls into the slice reconstruction so the result is a single self-contained R text.

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.autoReveal.markdownDescription: If there are less than or equal the given dependencies in the dependency view, reveal them automatically.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Update the dependency view on every change in the active editor.
Update on every change until the source becomes too big, then switch to interval.
Update the dependency view every n seconds, see `vscode-flowr.dependencyView.updateInterval`.
Update the dependency view only when the active editor is saved.
Never update the dependency view automatically.
vscode-flowr.dependencyView.updateType.markdownDescription: When to update the dependency view.

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.updateInterv.markdownDescription: Automatically update the dependency view every n seconds.

vscode-flowr.slice.revisitThreshold.markdownDescription: How often is flowR allowed to revisit, e.g., a function definition to infer more informations before it stops? Currently this only affects the internal session.

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.adaptiveChar.markdownDescription: The number of characters in the source after which the dependency view switches to interval updates.

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.cacheLimit.markdownDescription: The maximum number of dependency configurations to keep in the cache. This primarily improves the performance when you switch between files frequently (changing this clears the cache).

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.keepOnError.markdownDescription: Should the dependency view freeze when the code contains errors? If so, it will automatically retry on the next update (see `vscode-flowr.dependencyView.updateType`).

vscode-flowr.values.hover.markdownDescription: Whether to show the resolved values (by flowR's domains) of variables when hovering over them in R files.

vscode-flowr.values.hover.resolve.markdownDescription: Whether to use flowR's basic value resolve when hovering over variables.

vscode-flowr.values.hover.dataFrames.markdownDescription: Whether to use flowR's more advanced data frame shape inference.

vscode-flowr.packageInfo.enabled.markdownDescription: Whether flowR provides hovers with package and function information, *Go to Definition* and *Find References* for R files. Turn this off to only use other language support for these (for example, the R extension).

vscode-flowr.completion.enabled.markdownDescription: Whether flowR suggests completions and signature help for functions of loaded packages, backed by the signature database. Disable if it gets in the way of your usual completions.

vscode-flowr.mcp.enabled.markdownDescription: Offer flowR's MCP server (`@eagleoutice/flowr-mcp`, started with `npx`) to the editor's MCP clients, e.g. Copilot's agent mode. Needs VS Code 1.101 or newer and Node 22 or newer, and is not available in the browser.

vscode-flowr.completion.alwaysAvailableP.markdownDescription: Packages whose functions are always suggested, even without a `library()`/`require()` call in the file. Defaults to `base` and R's other default-loaded packages.

vscode-flowr.completion.showS3Methods.markdownDescription: Whether to suggest dotted function names (e.g. `print.data.frame`, usually S3 methods) before you've typed the dot yourself. Off by default, so typing `print` only suggests `print` itself; typing `print.` still suggests `print.data.frame`.

vscode-flowr.symbols.enabled.markdownDescription: Provide symbols (outline, breadcrumbs, *Go to Symbol*) for assigned variables and functions, and for dependencies such as libraries, data, plots and outputs.

enumDescriptions: Only dependencies; the language server lists the assignments.
All symbols, including those the language server lists too.
No symbols.
vscode-flowr.symbols.withRLanguageServer.markdownDescription: Which symbols flowR provides while the R extension's language server ([REditorSupport.r](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r), needs R's `languageserver`) runs. Without it, flowR provides all symbols.

enumDescriptions: Only suggest what the R language server cannot know: functions, arguments and package names of packages that are not installed locally.
Suggest everything the signature database knows, even where that duplicates the R language server's suggestions.
Suggest nothing at all while the R language server is available.
vscode-flowr.completion.withRLanguageSer.markdownDescription: How flowR suggests while the R extension's language server ([REditorSupport.r](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r), which needs R's `languageserver` package) is available. That server completes from your actual R session, flowR from its signature database, which also covers packages you have not installed - so by default flowR only fills that gap. Has no effect when the R language server is unavailable, where flowR always suggests everything.

vscode-flowr.recording.enabled.markdownDescription: Records a timeline of everything you do (edits, selections, opened files, commands, diagnostics, ...) into a local JSON file, e.g. to capture minimal working examples for bug reports or to trace user behavior in studies. The recording is **only ever stored locally** and never uploaded. Disabling this setting finishes the current recording.

vscode-flowr.recording.acronym.markdownDescription: The acronym (e.g., a participant pseudonym) recordings are filed under: each recording is written to `<acronym>-<timestamp>.json`. Applies when the next recording starts.

vscode-flowr.recording.directory.markdownDescription: The local directory recordings are written to. If empty, the first workspace folder is used.

vscode-flowr.verboseLog.markdownDescription: Whether to use verbose logging while flowR is active (this will also redirect flowR logs to the output panel).

vscode-flowr.debug.flowrLogLevel.markdownDescription: What logging level should flowR use?

vscode-flowr.errorMessage.Timer.markdownDescription: The time in milliseconds after which an error message will be removed from the status bar.

vscode-flowr.config.ignoreSourceCalls.markdownDescription: Whether source calls should be ignored when analyzing code, causing files sourced using the `source` function to be skipped.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Use alias tracking to resolve values.
Only resolve directly assigned builtin constants.
vscode-flowr.config.solver.variableHandl.markdownDescription: How to resolve variables and their values when analyzing code.

vscode-flowr.config.solver.resolveSource.markdownDescription: Find sourced files ignoring their capitalization?

enumDescriptions: Do not infer the working directory
Use the main script used for the analysis for the working directory
Use the active (sourced) script for the working directory
Consider all loaded scripts for the working directory
vscode-flowr.config.solver.resolveSource.markdownDescription: Which working directory to assume when resolving sourced files?
Which (additional) paths should be used to resolve sourced files?

enumDescriptions: Do not drop any parts of the path from a source
Drop the full path and only keep the filename if the path is not found.
Try every sub path in a source until a file is found.
vscode-flowr.config.solver.resolveSource.markdownDescription: How to handle paths in sources that are not found.

vscode-flowr.config.overwriteBuiltIns.lo.markdownDescription: When overwriting the builtin definitions of flowR, should the default configuration still be loaded?

vscode-flowr.config.overwriteBuiltIns.de.markdownDescription: When overwriting the builtin definitions of flowR, the set of additional definitions to load. For more info on how these need to be formatted, see [the wiki](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Interface#%EF%B8%8F-configuring-flowr).

vscode-flowr.config.solver.sigdb.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable the flowR signature database to resolve package exports and function signatures. When enabled, flowr loads precomputed signature databases for base R and CRAN packages.

vscode-flowr.config.solver.sigdb.autoSyn.markdownDescription: Automatically check for and download changed signature database shards in the background on startup. Off by default since it requires network access; use "Sync Signature Databases" in the Signature DB view to sync manually.

vscode-flowr.config.solver.sigdb.eagerly.markdownDescription: Load all base R packages and most-downloaded packages from the signature database up front. Enabling this makes the very first analysis slightly faster at the cost of some work during startup.

vscode-flowr.config.solver.sigdb.customP.markdownDescription: Optional path to a custom signature database file or directory to use **in addition to** the bundled default (flowR's `solver.sigdb.additionalPaths`). Leave empty to only use the shipped database. Automatically set after using "Sync Signature Databases" in the Signature DB view.

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.query.ignore.markdownDescription: When using the dependency view, should the set of functions that are detected by default be ignored/skipped?

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.query.overri.markdownDescription: When using the dependency view, the set of additional `libraryFunctions`, `sourceFunctions`, `readFunctions` and `writeFunctions` to load. For more info on how these need to be formatted, see [the wiki](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Query-API#dependencies-query).

enumDescriptions: Libraries
Imported Data
Sourced Scripts
Outputs
Visualizations
Tests
Statistical Tests
Remote Installs
Data Transformations

vscode-flowr.dependencyView.query.enable.markdownDescription: When using the dependency view, which dependency categories should be detected. Can also be toggled by right-clicking on a category in the dependency view itself.

enumDescriptions: Marks deprecated functions that should not be used anymore.
Checks whether file paths used in read/write operations point to existing files.
Checks whether randomness-based calls are preceded by a random seed (e.g. set.seed).
Checks whether file paths are absolute.
Checks for unused definitions.
Checks whether symbols conform to a certain naming convention (off by default).
Marks network functions (downloads, HTTP requests, etc.).
Validates existence of accessed columns/rows of dataframes.
Marks areas of code never reached during execution.
Detects loops which only iterate once.
Detects dynamic calls (eval, system) with non-constant inputs and pipe-command injection in graphics devices.
Checks whether stop calls set call. to FALSE.
Checks whether a function has undocumented or overdocumented parameters.
Checks whether the project provides a license.
Checks whether the project has tests.
Detects hardcoded credentials (experimental).
Flags calls to functions that are neither defined locally, a known builtin, nor exported by a loaded package (experimental).
Reports syntax errors the parser had to recover from, with quick fixes where possible (off by default).
Highlights packages that are attached but never used (requires the signature database).
Flags connections that are opened but not closed on every path.
Detects unescaped arguments to critical system, evaluation, database and HTML/JavaScript calls.
Flags pkg:::name where pkg::name would do, and pkg::name for names pkg does not export.
R CMD check: flags `if`/`while` conditions comparing `class(x)` with a string, with `inherits()` as a quick fix (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks the fields, version, maintainer, license and style of the DESCRIPTION (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds undocumented exports and functions whose formals differ from their Rd `\usage` and `\arguments` (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds non-ASCII characters in code and the NAMESPACE outside of comments, with `\u` escapes as a quick fix (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds `T` and `F` used for `TRUE` and `FALSE` (off by default, R packages only).
R CMD check: finds a bare `return` without `()`, with `return()` as a quick fix (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks `.onLoad`, `.onAttach`, `.onDetach` and `.Last.lib` (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds code that changes the global environment, e.g. `assign()` into it, `attach()` or `<<-` (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds `unlockBinding()` and `assignInNamespace()` on other namespaces and `.Internal()` calls (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds S3 methods whose formals do not match their generic or that are not registered (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks `.Call`, `.C`, `.External` and `.Fortran` calls (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds packages used but not declared in the DESCRIPTION, and declared imports never used (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds calls with arguments the called function does not take, or that match its formals only partially (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks the package files, e.g. portable names, hidden files, sizes and line endings (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks `src/` and the build files, e.g. non-portable Makevars flags (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks the demo index, `INDEX`, `inst/CITATION`, and links in README, NEWS and vignettes (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks the Rd files, e.g. syntax, sections, cross-references and examples (R packages only).
R CMD check: checks `data/` and `R/sysdata.rda` (R packages only).
R CMD check: finds what makes installing, loading or running the package fail, e.g. undefined exports (R packages only).

vscode-flowr.linter.enabledRules.markdownDescription: The names of the linting rules that should be enabled. See [the wiki](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Linter#linting-rules) for a list of linting rules and their identifiers. By default, all rules except `naming-convention`, `roxygen-arguments`, `syntactically-valid` and `true-false-abbreviation` are enabled. The rules ported from `R CMD check` (and `software-has-license`/`software-has-tests`) only run on files inside an R package. An empty array causes _all_ linting rules (including those four) to be enabled.

vscode-flowr.linter.ruleConfigs.markdownDescription: Custom configurations for enabled linting rules. See [the wiki](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr/wiki/Linter#linting-rules) for a list of linting rules and their configurations. Entries should use rule names as keys and configurations as values, for example: `{ "naming-convention": { "caseing": "snake_case" } }`.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Update the linter on every change in the active editor.
Update on every change until the source becomes too big, then switch to interval.
Update the linter every n seconds, see `vscode-flowr.linter.updateInterval`.
Update the linter only when the active editor is saved.

vscode-flowr.linter.updateInterval.markdownDescription: Automatically update the linter every n seconds (used by adaptive and interval).

vscode-flowr.linter.adaptiveCharacterLim.markdownDescription: The number of characters in the source after which the linter switches to interval updates.

vscode-flowr.diagram.sync.markdownDescription: If set to true, mermaid diagrams are automatically synced to the selected lines of code in the respective editor by default

markdownEnumDescriptions: Selected lines are highlighted in the diagram
Only selected lines are shown in the diagram
Simplification passes that should be applied to the cfg diagram

vscode-flowr.diagram.simplifyCfg.markdownDescription: If set to true, cfg diagrams are simplified

vscode-flowr.diagram.simplifyDfg.markdownDescription: If set to true, dfg diagrams are simplified

viewsWelcome.contents:
Welcome to flowR!
Open an R file to see its dependencies.

scripts.vscode:prepublish: npm run package && npm run package-web
scripts.copy-wasm-node: mkdir -p dist/node && cp node_modules/web-tree-sitter/tree-sitter.wasm dist/node && cp node_modules/@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r/tree-sitter-r.wasm dist/node
scripts.copy-wasm-web: mkdir -p dist/web && cp node_modules/web-tree-sitter/tree-sitter.wasm dist/web && cp node_modules/@davisvaughan/tree-sitter-r/tree-sitter-r.wasm dist/web
scripts.compile-tests: npm run compile && tsc -p . --outDir out && mkdir -p out/sigdb && cp node_modules/@eagleoutice/flowr/data/sigdb/sigdb.remote.json out/sigdb/
scripts.pretest: npm run compile-tests && npm run lint
scripts.package-web: webpack --mode production --devtool hidden-source-map --config-name web && node scripts/fetch-web-sigdb.mjs
